## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* is the sixteenth and concluding section of the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 16) in the Khuddaka Nikāya, providing a detailed canonical commentary on the *Sāriputta Sutta* [SuttaCentral]. In modern grammatical and chronological studies of canonical Pali literature, the text is cited for its distinctive verbal morphology, including aorist forms derived from the root *budh* such as *bujjhi*, *anubujjhi*, *paṭibujjhi*, *sambujjhi*, and *sammābujjhi* [Kingsbury 2002].
SuttaCentral records numerous passage-level parallels between the *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* and other early exegetical and doctrinal treatises, notably companion sections of the *Mahāniddesa* (such as the *Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa*, *Purābhedasuttaniddesa*, and *Attadaṇḍasuttaniddesa*), the *Cūḷaniddesa* (including the *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa*, *Mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa*, and *Pārāyanānugītigāthāniddesa*), the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, and the *Vibhaṅga* [SuttaCentral]. In addition, shared passages connect with suttas such as the *Sabbāsava Sutta* (MN 2) and *Āsavasutta* (AN 6.58), the *Nettippakaraṇa*, and various recensions of the *Dharmapada* / *Udānavarga* tradition across Pali, Sanskrit, Gāndhārī, and Chinese [SuttaCentral].
This extensive shared stock of formulaic and exegetical phrasing is corroborated by DharmaNexus computational analysis, which records widespread Pali-internal reuse—most prominently with the *Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 14), *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23), the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), the commentary *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā*, and Buddhaghosa's *Visuddhimagga* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of the text with non-Pali corpora, detecting matches with the Sanskrit and Tibetan recensions of the *Śrāvakabhūmi* in the *Yogācārabhūmi*, the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and its commentary, the *Patna Dharmapada*, and Prajñāpāramitā texts [DharmaNexus].
